content_html:
Why did the concept of ‘spiritual’ evolve?

Cognitive, Emotional, and Social Pathways

A concept map linking cognition (agency detection, ToM, memory), emotion (awe, mortality), and social evolution (ritual, costly signals, cohesion).

The ‘Spiritual’ can be seen as an emergent abstraction: from concrete spirits to relational principles (meaning, emptiness, unity), and it has many aspects:

Hyperactive Agency Detection (HADD): Bias toward seeing agents in ambiguity; safer false positives → seeds belief in unseen agents.

Theory of Mind → Invisible Minds: Extends mentalising beyond the visible to ancestors/gods/spirits; human mentalising extends to non-present minds.

Constructive Memory & Imagination: Past–future simulation enables unseen causal stories; remembering and imagining share neural machinery; enables supernatural narratives.

Awe & Altered States: “Vastness + need for accommodation” → small self, openness to meaning; emotion of vastness promotes prosociality and openness to transcendent frames.

Mortality Salience: Awareness of death motivates worldviews promising meaning/immortality; terror management dynamics, worldviews buffer death anxiety.

Ritual & Costly Signalling: High-cost practices as credible signals prove commitment, stabilise cooperation.

Group Cohesion & Transmission: Shared symbols, taboos, narratives → ritual fusion & identification increase group coordination → durable cultural memory
